svg.aria-label: Diagram: CloudWatch Logs PutAccountPolicy creates six kinds of account-level policy with one API call: data protection, subscription filter, field index, transformer, metric extraction and retention. Account-level policies are Region-specific, applying only to log groups in the Region where they are created. The conflict-resolution rule between an account-level policy and a log-group-level policy is different for each type. Data protection policies are cumulative, so any sensitive term specified in either policy is masked. Account-level and log-group-level subscription filters are additive, with up to one account-level and up to five log-group-level filters on a log group. A log-group-level transformer overrides the account-level transformer entirely. For field indexes, a log-group-level policy causes any account-level policy using log group name prefix criteria or no criteria to be ignored for that log group, while account-level policies using data source name and type criteria still apply alongside it. Metric extraction policies are account-level only and have no log-group equivalent. Retention inverts the pattern: an account-level retention policy replaces the retention period set on a log group, including when the log group's own period is longer, so a log group set to ten years under a new ninety-day policy has its older events deleted. Retention is also the only type with a dry run, which reports how many log groups would have decreased, increased or unchanged retention, and the only type whose selection criteria may overlap, where the longest retention period wins and never-expire counts as longest. Selection criteria differ per type: subscription filters support only log group name NOT IN a list, transformers only a log group name prefix, field indexes a prefix or a data source name and type, retention a prefix only, and data protection none at all, while metric extraction supports names and prefixes with IN and NOT IN operators. Account retention policies require a minimum of thirty days, take effect twenty-four hours after creation, and support retroactive or new-only enforcement, where new-only applies the policy only to log groups created after it. Disabling embedded metric format through a metric extraction policy also disables Container Insights and Application Signals metrics, so the documentation recommends excluding those log group prefixes. The permission to call this API should go only to administrators who manage logging configuration across the account.
svg.title: One API, six policy types, and six different precedence rules
svg.text: One API, six products. The precedence rule is different for every one.
“Account-level policies are Region-specific: a policy applies only to log groups in the Region where you
create it.” So every count below, and every gap, is per Region.
When an account policy meets a log-group policy
data protection cumulative — terms from both are masked
subscription filter additive — 1 account-level + up to 5 log-group-level
transformer the log group wins; the account policy is ignored
field index prefix-scoped ignored; data-source ones still apply
metric extraction no log-group equivalent exists
retention the ACCOUNT policy replaces the log group’s setting
Five rows say the log group keeps what it has. The sixth deletes.
“if a log group is set to retain log events for 10 years and you create a retention policy that sets a 90-day
retention period for that log group, CloudWatch Logs deletes the log events … older than 90 days.”
Nothing else in this API removes data. A team’s deliberate ten years loses to someone else’s prefix match.
WHAT EACH TYPE LETS YOU SELECT
subscription LogGroupName NOT IN [] (exclude only)
transformer LogGroupNamePrefix (include only)
field index prefix OR data source name+type
retention prefix · data protection: none at all
Whether you can exclude depends on which policy you write.
RETENTION’S OWN RULES
Overlap is allowed — longest period wins.
NEVER_EXPIRE counts as longest.
Minimum 30 days. Takes effect after 24 hours.
NEW_ONLY sets a future standard. RETROACTIVE
edits the past. This is the field that matters.
The dry run exists for exactly one of the six
“Specifying dryRun is valid only when you specify RETENTION_POLICY for policyType.” It reports how many
log groups lose retention, gain it, or stay the same — and the decreased count is the data you are deleting.
Also: a metric extraction policy that disables EMF switches off Container Insights and Application Signals
unless you exclude their prefixes — a cost control removing an observability feature two layers away.
Read policyType as choosing a different product, not a different mode.
